effect_mechanism: Putting tree cover back on cleared or degraded land rebuilds the structure that forest species need, and then lets dispersers do the rest. Measured against degraded ecosystems across 221 study landscapes worldwide, forest restoration enhanced biodiversity by 15-84% and vegetation structure by 36-77% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1]. How the cover is re-established changes the result: natural regeneration surpassed active restoration for plants, birds and invertebrates, with restoration success 34 to 56% higher after controlling for forest cover, precipitation and time [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1]. Recovery is a function of time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], and the clock is slow — a secondary Atlantic forest was estimated to need 65 years, with a range of 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. What accelerates it is anything that brings seed in or keeps grazing out: beneath framework-species plantings, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]; artificial perches brought native zoochoric regeneration that was absent from the planted rings [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2]; and Senegalese exclosures carried 27 woody species after a year against 51 in the 5- and 12-year enclosures, more than 52% higher richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1]. In mangroves, restored stands held higher crab production and diversity than degraded ones [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_1]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta an independent evaluation relays that forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, and that in the zones around protected mangrove roots sea crabs and shellfish re-appeared in some places and increased in others [ev_frmg_vnppar_3, ev_frmg_vnppar_4]. Practitioners implementing these technologies in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, India, Niger and Turkmenistan record plant, animal and habitat diversity rising as cover returns and protection holds [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4300_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The other route is keeping the forest that exists, since the governance instruments that retain cover also hold the habitat: GEF sustainable forest management sites lost about 0.27% less forest each year than matched areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], payments improved forest cover and reduced deforestation in pooled analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2], and participatory management is credited with regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2].
conditionality: Planting is not automatically the better route, and in some settings it is the worse one. Where forests can regenerate naturally or with some assistance, reforestation based on tree planting can actually reduce biodiversity conservation benefits if the selected species or management do not provide suitable habitat for species of conservation concern [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]; plantation after regeneration cutting gave lower species richness than natural regeneration, on very few cases and with a very imprecise estimate [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. Measured against an uncut control forest, plantations lost 40% of local species richness and clear-cut followed by natural regeneration lost 22% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_3]. That comparison is a stand still recovering towards the forest that stood there, which is incomplete recovery against an intact reference rather than damage done by restoration; the gains in this row are measured from cleared, degraded or grazed starting points, and the two baselines must not be mixed. Several outcomes did not move: biodiversity in Vietnamese special-use forests showed no clear-cut evidence of a positive project impact, with the tracking tool judged an unsuitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1]; restored mangroves showed no major difference from unvegetated tidal flats for fish and crab production and diversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_2]; management transfer under Madagascar's Gelose remained superficial and did not stop clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2]; and broadleaf crown-cover change under Van Panchayats was insignificant [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2]. Harm was measured too, though rarely: of 1,924 project locations assessed, 33 (1.7%) showed strong evidence of negative outcomes, all apparently in areas susceptible to urban encroachment, and 169 (8.7%) gave no evidence of a positive outcome [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]. Two things qualify the strength. Much of the positive weight comes from practitioner ratings on a fixed scale and from forest-cover and governance findings routed in as a component proxy, not from direct biodiversity counts [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. And the benefit is not costless on the farm: a compiler who rated wildlife increasing also recorded that this led to danger of wild life on crops and domestic animals [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The return of crabs and shellfish is an anecdotal observation, and it came with protection contracts given to smallholders as well as the replanting [ev_frmg_vnppar_4].

effect_mechanism: This row rests on forest-governance evidence pooled across several countries, with forest cover standing in for habitat. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) compared with areas without payments [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]. World Bank participatory forest management projects reported reduced deforestation rates, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity where those outcomes were monitored, and Bank-supported payment schemes had a positive effect on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas, which limits what they deliver for biodiversity [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. Most units measure forest cover or deforestation, a component proxy for biodiversity, not species. The pooled payment effects come from a systematic review and meta-analysis, while the World Bank units are evaluation narratives that cover only projects that monitored outcomes; all concern keeping or managing existing forest through payments or community management rather than restoration planting.

effect_mechanism: In these upper-middle-income settings the evidence is about succession on land that has been cleared or degraded, and about what speeds it up. Tree species richness rose as a function of time since disturbance across an Atlantic rainforest chronosequence [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], with a forest estimated to need 65 years, range 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. Assisted recruitment shortens the wait: beneath framework-species plantings in Thai dry forest, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and artificial perches produced native zoochoric regenerants that were absent from planted rings, so bringing in dispersers mattered more than the planting itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1]. On Turkmen barkhan sands the revegetated area is recorded as providing habitat for 25-27 species of plants and animals, with plant and animal diversity rated as increasing [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. Holding the cover is the companion mechanism: under community forest management in the Sierra Norte de Puebla, forest cover did not decline after the handover but increased by 8% [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta an independent evaluation relays that forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, and that in the zones around protected mangrove roots sea crabs and shellfish re-appeared in some places and increased in others [ev_frmg_vnppar_3, ev_frmg_vnppar_4].
conditionality: The direction is consistent, but the base is thin and soft: chronosequences and site studies, a set of compiler ratings, and a forest-cover change read from land-use maps as a proxy for habitat rather than a count of species [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Where a project was independently evaluated the result was less flattering — biodiversity is hard to assess, the management-effectiveness tool used was not a suitable proxy, and there was no clear-cut evidence that a Vietnamese special-use forest project had a positive impact [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1]. Time is the binding condition: the Atlantic-forest estimate spans decades to well over a century before the assemblage approaches the composition of a mature forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2], so nothing here promises a measurable result inside a project cycle. Two reading rules apply. The gains are measured against the degraded or cleared starting point, not against intact forest, and a young stand holding less than old-growth is incomplete recovery rather than loss. And the perch and framework-species findings are about assisting dispersal into a restoration site [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]: they presuppose a seed source within reach, which is a siting condition a scan can test and a restoration in a cleared landscape may fail. effect_mechanism: Restoration accumulates carbon in two pools: biomass as the trees grow, and soil organic carbon after the land-use transition. On biomass, planted forests and woodlots had the highest removal rates at 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2 per hectare per year during the first 20 years of growth, mangrove tree restoration came second at up to 23.1 and then 10.5 over the following 40 years, and natural regeneration removed 9.1 to 18.8 [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_4, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_3]. effect_mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

effect_mechanism: Young planted trees use a lot of water, and streamflow falls. Because of high water use by young, densely spaced trees, forest plantations of native species aged 25 to 45 years produce persistent dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to native old-growth forests [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3]. Afforesting grasslands and shrublands reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and 31%, with proportionally larger reductions for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4], and afforestation is noted to reduce water yield while providing erosion benefits [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more. A loss here can coexist with a local gain in the active-planting water stress row, since young dense trees use much of the water [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3]. The comparator in the Pacific Northwest figure is old-growth forest, not the land the plantation replaced. A cited review found most studies reported decreases in water yield after forestation, but most referred to plantation forestry rather than restoration with mostly slower-growing native species [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_1] — the main reason not to carry the size of this loss straight onto native-species restoration. The modelled units point the other way at landscape scale: under full reforestation potential by mid-century, water yield rose significantly in four regions, by 11.4%, 16.9%, 17.6% and 84.9% [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_2, ev_water_regulation_teo22_3, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4], while some other regions show nonsignificant declines where heightened evapotranspiration outstrips the increase in precipitation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_5]. Expect the largest proportional losses in the driest catchments [ev_water_yield_farley05_4].

effect_mechanism: Reforestation slows storm runoff and lowers flood peaks in catchment models: in Slovakia's Hornad watershed a 50% increase of forest cut a simulated flood peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and reduced peaks by about 24% on average in rain-duration tests, more for short storms than long ones [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and an afforestation simulation for Luxembourg's Alzette basin decreased the peak by 8% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. A systematic review found that flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of studies reporting them [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde, Uganda and Bosnia and Herzegovina, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan, mangrove buffers in the Philippines, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and a learning site in Afghanistan rate downstream flooding or flood impacts as reduced; an Ethiopian compiler notes that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced, and the Afghan compiler that riverbanks were revegetated with communities planting cuttings along banks and shorelines [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts]. On the coast, 50% of the mangrove restoration projects in a global review state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events, and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports higher restoration cost-benefit ratios once the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

Both are expert positions rather than measurements, the FAO–CIFOR statement citing earlier work. effect_mechanism: Mangrove belts lower coastal flood impact by attenuating waves and, far more weakly, storm-surge water levels as water passes through the forest, with attenuation depending on inundation depth, tree species, density and the presence of creeks [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3]. Observed wave-height attenuation reaches 1.2% per m of mangrove and gravity-wave energy falls by up to 75% over a few tens of metres, while surface wind waves are expected to be reduced by more than 75% over a kilometre of mangroves; tidal and trans-tidal attenuation is two orders of magnitude smaller, up to 2 cm per 100 m [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_2, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_2]. Measured storm-surge peak water level reduction ranges from 5 to 50 centimetres per kilometre of mangrove width, and a hurricane surge attenuation rate of 9.4 cm/km has been measured over relatively continuous mangrove forest in Southern Florida, slightly lower along a river corridor [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1, ev_frmg_leon17_1], and a validated model put Hurricane Wilma inundation at 4,220 km2 without mangroves against 2,450 km2 with them [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_5]. The consequences for people and property follow: a global flood model finds that if current mangroves were lost, 29% more land, 28% more people and 9% more property would be damaged every year, with benefits broadly consistent across return periods [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_2, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_3]; in Orissa, India, mangroves reduced the average number of cyclone deaths in villages within 10km of the coast by 69%, and the village protected by mangroves had the lowest storm-surge loss per household [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_10, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_9]. In Bangladesh a cited model finds 500 m afforestation patches can mitigate current velocities up to 90% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2], and WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. The avoided damage has also been monetised: in Orissa, mangroves provided house-protection benefits of USD 1218 per hectare of forest in a single super cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and in Thailand storm protection accounted for US$ 8,966-10,821 per hectare, about 87% of estimated mangrove value, with the long-term total economic value of an intact mangrove swamp about 3.6 times that of converting it to shrimp aquaculture [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2]. A meta-analysis of field measurements finds that existing mangroves reduce wave heights by 31% (95% CI: 25–37%) [ev_frmg_nara16_1]. Of mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events, and a cited economic model for northern Vietnam gives restoration scenarios higher cost-benefit ratios once the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is counted [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].
conditionality: The monetised figures are society-wide avoided damage - averted property loss and protection service valued wherever it falls - and not income reaching the rural households a World Bank investment targets, so they say what the hazard protection is worth, not what the practice pays its adopters [ev_economic_return_das11_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2]. That value does not settle the land-use case: in Orissa the value of coastal land in alternate uses far exceeds the value mangroves provide by protecting residential property, and on that information alone mangrove conservation or rehabilitation could not be justified [ev_economic_return_das11_2]; the same Orissa figure is a single-event amount with no stated price year and is not annualised [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and the Thai values are model estimates cited in a review, the larger of them covering timber, non-timber products and fisheries as well as coastal protection [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2]. Most of the units here, measured and modelled alike, describe existing mangrove forest rather than restored stands, including the global model, whose counterfactual is the loss of current mangroves rather than new planting, so the step from standing forest to a restoration investment is assumed rather than evidenced [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_2, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_3, ev_economic_return_marois15_1]. Protection is also conditional on width and on what dominates the water level: the Bangladesh study finds mangroves have a small effect (<4%) on total water level because the design level is dominated by the surge, which is unaffected by mangroves in that model [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2]. On evidence quality, the measured surge reductions all come from south Florida in the USA, the wind-wave reduction is derived from small-wave rather than storm measurements, the Orissa household-loss comparison is a perception-based survey of a handful of villages, much of the review material is cited secondary rather than new measurement, and the WOCAT entries are compiler ratings [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_2, ev_frmg_leon17_1, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_9, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. The wave and surge figures measure what standing mangroves do, not what planting achieves: the wave meta-analysis covers existing habitat, measured under ‘normal’ conditions of low waves, and the Florida surge rates are measurements over existing forest [ev_frmg_nara16_1, ev_frmg_leon17_1]. That a planted stand will deliver the same is assumed, not measured, in these units. The restoration-project share counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured, and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a second-hand reading of the model [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

effect_mechanism: This row describes the flood regulation that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. A country-level analysis of developing countries predicted that a further hypothetical 10% loss of natural forest cover would raise flood frequency by 3.5% to 28.1% and flood duration by 3.8% to 7.9% [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_1, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_2]. At the local scale forests and forest soils reduce runoff through enhanced infiltration and storage, and peak flows rise after forest removal in small experimental catchments [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_2]. In Malaysia an analysis with adequate controls for confounding factors found flood risk increased after natural forest was converted to plantation crops and urban land [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_1], in the USA forest harvest was associated with significant increases in peak flows in both small and large (100 - 1,000 km2) basins [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_3], and in Swiss valleys with more than 30% forest snowmelt was more gradual and flooding risk lower [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_2]. At a learning site in Afghanistan the compiler rates flood impacts as decreased after riverbanks were revegetated through control measures [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
conditionality: The service fades with storm size and basin size. Forest soils reduce runoff only in small-scale rainfall events, which are not responsible for severe downstream flooding, and forests cannot stop catastrophic large-scale floods caused by severe meteorological events [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_2]; small to medium peak flows are affected most while the largest events do not change noticeably, and studies in larger basins have not usually found changes after deforestation of up to 50% of the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_3, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_4]; and in the Himalaya tree cutting was not the reason for flooding in the downstream plains [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_4]. The cross-country analysis itself found little evidence that further forest loss changed flood deaths or damage [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_3, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_4], and a reanalysis of its data found the correlation between forest cover or cover loss and flood frequency appears absent, with the degraded-lands fraction accounting for most of the variation [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_1]. The literature is contested: the two country-level statistical analyses disagree, the FAO–CIFOR and van Dijk statements are expert syntheses, the Malaysian, US and Swiss results are secondary citations in a global assessment, and all compare forest with cleared or less-forested land, so they show what losing forest costs rather than the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme. The Afghanistan unit is a practitioner rating from a learning site that bundles several land and forest management practices [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].

effect_mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases, community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]; in Costa Rica, payments for reforestation made up 18.66% of participants' income, against about 10% of family income in other Latin American programmes [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Mangrove planting in Viet Nam raised shell and oyster yields per hectare, with benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits, and a global meta-analysis gives mangrove restoration benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_su21_1]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes, and plantations would be profitable without carbon payments across 28.3% of the plantation-feasible area [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2, ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1]. Two mangrove appraisals point the same way: a second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable from an economic perspective based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and in Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, the Ugandan compiler rates it unchanged, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, an implementer-commissioned evaluation in Viet Nam, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), perception scores (the Costa Rica economic impact of 63.9%), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2, ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_padilla17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Vietnam's plantation return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and its gains rested on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1], Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group. The Vietnam model is cited second-hand and described by the citing author as preliminary [ev_frmg_erw09_1]. The Mexico result is the project's own completion report, and its benefits are projected forward from planting on former cattle pasture rather than observed; coastal protection and carbon were not valued [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. Two cost findings are kept out of the direction because the saving goes to society rather than to households: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against submerged breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, and depending on the water depth, mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. That comparison assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, rests on wave reduction measured under normal low-wave conditions, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective.

effect_mechanism: What is left in this row is evidence on costs and on benefits that reach people: mangrove planting supports coastal livelihoods mainly through aquatic products, and the returns on the planting itself are reported as benefit-cost ratings. In northern Viet Nam a community mangrove plantation raised per-hectare yields of aquaculture products such as shells and oysters by 209-789 per cent, providing additional income for coastal communities [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1], and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A global meta-analysis of mangrove restoration reports a benefit-cost ratio of 3.36 to 2.19 across discount rates when using the mean value of estimated total economic benefits [ev_economic_return_su21_1], a cited study concludes that the benefits of mangrove reforestation projects outweigh their costs [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1], and in Orissa, India, a comparison of costs and benefits found protecting the remaining mangroves economically justified against the forgone agricultural land [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate food security and self-sufficiency in Senegal and the risk of production failure in Bangladesh as improved, and rate the long-term cost-benefit of both establishment and maintenance as positive [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD/ha, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD/ha [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Two mangrove appraisals point the same way: a second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable from an economic perspective based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and in Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
conditionality: Monetised avoided storm damage no longer sits in this row: it is hazard protection whose value accrues to society at large rather than income reaching the targeted households, and it is accounted under coastal flood hazard instead. What remains is thin on direct measurement of poverty. Nothing here observes household income or poverty against a counterfactual: the outcome is reached only through proxies - economic return, food security and reported income gains - and the strongest cost-benefit numbers are project appraisals rather than measured welfare [ev_economic_return_su21_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]. The Viet Nam figures come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model costs and benefits forward, and the higher ratios include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples and is dominated by East and Southeast Asian planting projects [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; the Bangladesh livelihood values are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed income, and come from grey literature with the positive bias that carries [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The Orissa comparison concerns retaining existing mangroves rather than restoring new ones, and its own quote notes that the government's early warning evidently saved more lives than mangroves did [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1]. Several of the units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements, and the review finding is a conclusion cited from another study rather than a result of its own [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. The Vietnam model is cited second-hand and described by the citing author as preliminary [ev_frmg_erw09_1]. The Mexico result is the project's own completion report, and its benefits are projected forward from planting on former cattle pasture rather than observed; coastal protection and carbon were not valued [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. Two cost findings are kept out of the direction because the saving goes to society rather than to households: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against submerged breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, and depending on the water depth, mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. That comparison assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, rests on wave reduction measured under normal low-wave conditions, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective.

effect_mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income, employment and food from forests. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases [ev_household_income_iufro20_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand and, in large studies controlling for socio-economic factors, drove poverty reduction [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1]: a meta-analysis of counterfactual studies finds small positive effects of protected areas on local monetary outcomes (g = 0.028) and poverty outcomes (g = 0.117) [ev_household_income_kandel22_1, ev_rural_poverty_kandel22_1], households in the Chitwan National Park buffer zone of Nepal have 19 percent higher per capita income [ev_household_income_kandel22_2], and across developing countries living within 10 km of protected areas with documented tourism lowers the likelihood of poverty by 16.1% and of child stunting by 13.4%, with poverty 8.8% lower near multiple-use protected areas even without tourism [ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_1, ev_food_security_naidoo19_1, ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_2]. Exposure to standing forest feeds children: high forest exposure gives at least 25% greater dietary diversity in sub-Saharan Africa [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_1, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_2, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_3, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_4], child dietary diversity rises with community tree cover across 21 African countries, and in Malawi children in communities that experienced deforestation had less diverse diets [ev_food_security_iufro15_2, ev_food_security_iufro15_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management raised participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, poorer households compensated for lost land access gained 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1], households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1], in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1], non-timber income rose after benefit-sharing at Bach Ma, Vietnam [ev_household_income_ieg18_3], and WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate food self-sufficiency and long-term returns as improved [ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_economic_return_wocat_5243_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long].

On the coast of Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta, project monitoring relayed by an independent evaluation reports that because of the replanted mangroves coastal erosion was reduced by 40 percent in Ca Mau and the length and area of coastline accreting increased by 20 percent, and the evaluation mission found that stabilising the beach with mangroves in Soc Trang has turned the coast into an accretion zone [ev_frmg_vnppar_1, ev_frmg_vnppar_2].

effect_mechanism: This row describes the slope stability that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: landslides begin to increase when roots decay at around three years after forest clearance and susceptibility remains high until around 15 years, rates of mass erosion on steep forested terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after timber harvesting, and in southeast Alaska the area affected by landslides after logging was 5 times greater than in a 100-year period before it [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis likewise notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil a certain amount of mechanical support, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The landslide units are forest-loss contrasts and expert consensus, largely from temperate regions and cited second-hand, so they show what clearing costs rather than measuring the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. The root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by the presence or absence of a well-developed forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2].
